thread:
sasha: Repro steps and quick traces for KV warmup jitter causing sustained memory growth on on-prem A100 nodes. Hosted/dedicated plateau, private keeps climbing. cc @jamie @tyler
jamie: Oof. Is this the longctx workload we saw earlier? Any perf profiles?
tyler: Yes. Repro script: `scripts/repro_kv_warmup.sh --model 13b --seq 4096 --iter 2500` on private node. Observed KV mem: 1.2GB -> 5.6GB over ~40 minutes. Hosted/dedicated: 1.2GB -> 1.6GB plateau.
li: Can you paste pmap/ps output? Also are we seeing many page faults?
sasha: Logs:
```
kv_alloc: tenant=abc shard=0 frames=3.2M -> resident=5.6M
major-faults: 120k
jemalloc: allocated 4.1G, active=4.5G, metadata=120MB
```
Perf sample: `perf record -g -- ./runtime --workload kvcache_warmup` shows hot paths in `kv_reclaim::try_evict` and `jemalloc:arena_alloc_easy`.
ops-bot: deploy-cpu-collector: finished run for 10m - traces at https://console.redwood/prof/kvcache/3776543210
olivia: On private we disabled hugetlb/shmem for testing last month. Could that explain the diff?
jamie: Possibly. Also private nodes still have older driver+kernel (5.10 vs 6.1) and default `vm.min_free_kbytes` is lower. That can make fragmentation worse under repeated mmap/munmap patterns.
tyler: We measured page-size mix with `cat /proc/meminfo | egrep 'HugePages|AnonHugePages'` — private showed 0 reserved hugepages; hosted had hugetlb backing some shared memory we rely on for KV.
sasha: Key observation: when batch size oscillates (sometimes 1 token, sometimes 32), the runtime does many small KV frame allocations then evictions, leaving holes. jemalloc arenas on NUMA later can't satisfy large contiguous requests so we fall back to mmap -> more fragmentation.
li: Any cgroup differences? hosted uses per-tenant memcg, dedicated uses reserved slab, private uses default systemd cgroups?
tyler: Private runs in our lab VMs without our memcg tuning: no memory.high, no hard limits, so fragmentation can grow unchecked and kernel won't reclaim the same way.
olivia: I reproduced quickly: toggling `MALLOC_CONF` to `oversize_threshold:1,lg_chunk:0` reduced fragmentation a lot. Not sure it's safe cluster-wide though.
jamie: Short-term mitigations: 1) ship jemalloc config to private AMIs to reduce arenas/oversize, 2) add optional KV preallocation at startup to reserve contiguous frames, 3) kernel-side: enable hugetlb or bump `vm.min_free_kbytes` on on-prem test nodes.
sasha: Ran a canary: pre-allocating contiguous KV frames (simulate full 4096 seq) -> private plateaud same as hosted. So root cause appears to be warmup allocation pattern + lack of hugetlb rather than core kernel scheduler.
li: Let's add telemetry: per-tenant `kv_frag_ratio` + `longctx_growth_rate` and expose in console. Also add a runtime heuristic: when observed longctx token depth > X, switch to a steady batching policy to avoid oscillation.
tyler: Action items: @jamie add jemalloc config to private AMI (short-term), @sasha implement prealloc warmup option behind rollout flag, @olivia run hugetlb experiment on 2 on-prem nodes and report perf. I'll create tickets.
sasha: Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567 - warmup-prealloc option. Includes microbench results.
ops-bot: ticket created: INF-2391 kv-warmup-frag-private; assignees: jamie, sasha, olivia; due: 2026-04-02
jamie: :thumbsup: I'll add benchmark numbers + flamegraphs to the PR and schedule a short canary on dedicated nodes tomorrow.
